| **CN** | NEV majority | NEV retail penetration 2025 about 54.1% (Dec about 59–60%). Wholesale NEV mix: BEV 61.8%, PHEV 29.5%, EREV 8.7%. EREV demand rose late 2025 | [S47][S48] |
| CN | Premium segment shrinking | Over-RMB-300k sales −10% (Jan–Nov 2025). Premium share of market 14% (2024) to 13% (9M 2025) | [S49][S50] |
| CN | Domestic brands take the premium segment | Domestic share above RMB 300k: 24.9% (2023) to about 41% (2025), projected over 50% in 2026 **(U)**. Above RMB 300k NEV: over 80% domestic | [S51][S52] |
| CN | German brands declining | Mercedes CN 551,900 (−19%; another source: 472,799 **(conflict)**), BMW −12.5%, Audi 617k (−5.6%), Porsche −26% | [S1][S53][S49][S35] |

**Why Chinese premium brands take share from German brands in China (evidence):**

1. **Intelligent driving.** Chinese premium NEV buyers cite automated driving as the #1 purchase reason, ahead of smart cabin and styling [S54]. ADAS has up to 2× the purchase influence of Western markets, and 50% of Chinese shoppers would switch brand for better ADAS [S43]. "Insufficient intelligent driving experience" is cited for the BBA decline [S49].
2. **Smart cockpit and ecosystem.** Buyers expect phone-like UX, voice, and ecosystem integration (Huawei HarmonyOS, Xiaomi HyperOS). 45% of luxury owners say NEVs above RMB 300k need full smart connectivity [S54]. Even BMW's China Neue Klasse uses Momenta ADAS, Huawei HiCar and an Alibaba LLM [S5][S55].
3. **Brand heritage matters less.** Heritage only slightly outranks safety and handling as a premium definer, and matters less among high-income tier-1 buyers [S54][S56].
4. **Rear-seat luxury for the money.** The M9 and S800 offer zero-gravity seats, fridge, projector and 3.3 m+ wheelbases at prices below German flagships [S29][S6].
5. **Electrification gap.** BEV is only about 5% of BMW China sales against a 46% EV market [S54]. EREV/PHEV options give range without anxiety [S48].
6. **Innovation over discounts.** McKinsey: steep discounts gave marginal growth, and innovation wins [S56].

| Tech must *work* | Reliability and usability beat feature count. China TXI: 10.7 problems per 100 per advanced feature; over a third are cockpit usability. Recognition tech (gesture, face, fingerprint) disappoints. Smart climate and driver profiles score well | J.D. Power China TXI 2025, US TXI 2025 | [S57][S58] |
| Physical controls | Euro NCAP from 2026 rewards physical controls for indicators, hazards, wipers, horn and SOS. Infotainment is the #1 complaint area in the first 90 days. The F70 is criticised for moving climate controls onto the touchscreen and dropping the iDrive knob | Euro NCAP, reviews | [S59][S60] |
| ADAS | Strong switching driver: about 25% globally and 50% in China would switch brand for better self-driving; under-45s far more so (45+: 11%). US: partial automation has low perceived usefulness **(U)** | McKinsey Pulse 2026 | [S43][S58] |

Neue Klasse adds "Heart of Joy" (driving dynamics as the 4th pillar beside electric, digital, circular). Zipse: "Sheer Driving Pleasure – taken to a whole new level" | [S64][S65] |
| BMW (perceived) | Sportiness, driver focus, dynamics; M brand strong (213,457, record). Design controversies: big kidney grilles (XM, 7 Series, 4 Series), which BMW says were driven by China demand and that "complainers are often not customers". 7 Series facelift moves to horizontal slats | [S1][S66][S9] |
| **Mercedes** | Luxury, comfort, prestige, screens (Superscreen), rear-seat opulence (Maybach); leads on LLM assistant and illuminated design | [S34] |

### Brand-fit guardrails (for `fit_checks.brand`)

**All segments**
- **Fits BMW (pass):** precise steering and handling, rear-wheel-drive-biased feel and xDrive, responsive powertrains; driver-centric HMI (head-up display, Panoramic Vision, physical shortcut controls, iDrive-style haptic control); efficiency and range as "dynamics"; sporty-elegant design; M and M Performance variants; high-quality OTA and natural voice that *works*; ADAS that reduces burden while keeping the driver in charge.
- **Warn:** features that are "comfort-only" with no link to driving pleasure (acceptable but not differentiating); market-specific ecosystem partners (Huawei/Alibaba) acceptable in China only; grille-size escalation (polarising; region-specific).
- **Fail (contradicts the brand):** paywalling hardware already in the car (heated-seat precedent); touch-only access to core driving functions; soft, numb chassis tuning as default; gimmick recognition tech with no customer problem; copying the Chinese "living room on wheels" so far that the driver role is diminished in the 1 and 5 Series.

| Segment | Fits BMW (pass) | Warn | Contradicts (fail) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 Series** | Hot-hatch driving fun (M135), compact premium quality, intuitive physical controls, efficient BEV/PHEV option, youthful digital UX and app ecosystem | Pure value or feature stuffing to fight Chinese entrants; FWD-only perception | Cheap interior trim; touch-only climate (already criticised); losing dynamic edge vs Golf GTI |
| **5 Series / i5** | "Business athlete": dynamics plus long-distance comfort, top ADAS on the highway, fast charging and range, rear comfort in the China LWB, quiet cabin | China-only rear "boss" features in the G68 (pass for CN, warn for EU/US); third-party cockpit OS (CN only) | Sacrificing handling for float-ride everywhere; global commitment to an EREV range-extender identity **(PM judgement)** |
| **7 Series / i7** | Driver-*and*-chauffeur duality, Theatre Screen and rear lounge, Executive Lounge seats, craftsmanship, quiet BEV, L2+/L3 assisted driving | Matching Maextro/M9 gadgets one-for-one (fridge, projector) unless executed at BMW quality | Overt bling with no taste (grille-size controversy); dropping driving dynamics entirely (the S-Class owns pure comfort) |

**Status:** Seed v1. Researched 2026-10-10 via web search.
**Scope:** Successors of BMW 1 Series (F70), 5 Series (G60 / i5 / China LWB G68) and 7 Series (G70 / i7) in Europe (EU), China (CN) and the US.

**Conventions**
- `[S#]` refers to the source list at the end. Each source has a URL and a publication date.
- **(U)** marks something unverified: a single non-authoritative source, a figure that conflicts with another source, or general industry knowledge without a fetched source. Treat these items as evidence level E3/E4.
- Sales figures are calendar-year 2025 unless stated otherwise. Where sources disagree, both figures are shown.

## 2. Demand trends

| Market | Trend | Data | Src |
|---|---|---|---|
| **EU** | BEV rising, hybrids dominant | EU 2025: BEV 17.4% (from 13.6%), PHEV 9.4%, HEV 34.5%, petrol+diesel 35.5% (from 45.2%) | [S40] |
| EU | SUVs keep growing; sedans are a niche | SUV about 59.2% of 2025 sales; sedans 3.5% (about 426k); hatchbacks 23.9% (35% in 2020); wagons 7.1% | [S41] |
| EU | Premium mid-size sedans shrinking | Premium mid-size sedan category −19% Jan–Oct 2025 (241,096) | [S42] |
| EU | Chinese brands gaining | 6.1% share in 2025, 9.5% in Dec. 54% of Europeans see Chinese OEMs as EV leaders (2026, up from 44%) | [S18][S43] |
| **US** | BEV fell after the federal credit ended (30 Sep 2025) | BEV peaked at 12% in Sep 2025, then under 6% per month. HEV+BEV+PHEV about 22% in 2025. Q3 2026 forecast: about 6% EV | [S44][S45] |
| US | Affordability pressure | About 43% plan to delay purchase; 31% of premium buyers delaying. 89% of EV owners would buy another plug-in (70% EV, 19% PHEV) | [S43] |
| US | SUVs dominate | SUV/crossover about 58% of light vehicles; US LV sales 16.3M | [S46] |
| **CN** | NEV majority | NEV retail penetration 2025 about 54.1% (Dec about 59–60%). Wholesale NEV mix: BEV 61.8%, PHEV 29.5%, EREV 8.7%. EREV demand rose late 2025 | [S47][S48] |
| CN | Premium segment shrinking | Over-RMB-300k sales −10% (Jan–Nov 2025). Premium share of market 14% (2024) to 13% (9M 2025) | [S49][S50] |
| CN | Domestic brands take the premium segment | Domestic share above RMB 300k: 24.9% (2023) to about 41% (2025), projected over 50% in 2026 **(U)**. Above RMB 300k NEV: over 80% domestic | [S51][S52] |
| CN | German brands declining | Mercedes CN 551,900 (−19%; another source: 472,799 **(conflict)**), BMW −12.5%, Audi 617k (−5.6%), Porsche −26% | [S1][S53][S49][S35] |

**Why Chinese premium brands take share from German brands in China (evidence):**

1. **Intelligent driving.** Chinese premium NEV buyers cite automated driving as the #1 purchase reason, ahead of smart cabin and styling [S54]. ADAS has up to 2× the purchase influence of Western markets, and 50% of Chinese shoppers would switch brand for better ADAS [S43]. "Insufficient intelligent driving experience" is cited for the BBA decline [S49].
2. **Smart cockpit and ecosystem.** Buyers expect phone-like UX, voice, and ecosystem integration (Huawei HarmonyOS, Xiaomi HyperOS). 45% of luxury owners say NEVs above RMB 300k need full smart connectivity [S54]. Even BMW's China Neue Klasse uses Momenta ADAS, Huawei HiCar and an Alibaba LLM [S5][S55].
3. **Brand heritage matters less.** Heritage only slightly outranks safety and handling as a premium definer, and matters less among high-income tier-1 buyers [S54][S56].
4. **Rear-seat luxury for the money.** The M9 and S800 offer zero-gravity seats, fridge, projector and 3.3 m+ wheelbases at prices below German flagships [S29][S6].
5. **Electrification gap.** BEV is only about 5% of BMW China sales against a 46% EV market [S54]. EREV/PHEV options give range without anxiety [S48].
6. **Innovation over discounts.** McKinsey: steep discounts gave marginal growth, and innovation wins [S56].

## 3. General customer expectations 2025–2030 (premium)

| Theme | Expectation | Evidence | Src |
|---|---|---|---|
| Software / OTA | Car improves over time; AI and LLM voice assistants become standard (MB.OS on CLA and S, Alexa+ on 7 Series) | OEM launches 2025–26 | [S13][S34][S9] |
| Tech must *work* | Reliability and usability beat feature count. China TXI: 10.7 problems per 100 per advanced feature; over a third are cockpit usability. Recognition tech (gesture, face, fingerprint) disappoints. Smart climate and driver profiles score well | J.D. Power China TXI 2025, US TXI 2025 | [S57][S58] |
| Physical controls | Euro NCAP from 2026 rewards physical controls for indicators, hazards, wipers, horn and SOS. Infotainment is the #1 complaint area in the first 90 days. The F70 is criticised for moving climate controls onto the touchscreen and dropping the iDrive knob | Euro NCAP, reviews | [S59][S60] |
| ADAS | Strong switching driver: about 25% globally and 50% in China would switch brand for better self-driving; under-45s far more so (45+: 11%). US: partial automation has low perceived usefulness **(U)** | McKinsey Pulse 2026 | [S43][S58] |
| Charging / range | Fast charging valued even in lower-priced cars (CN). Benchmarks: CLA 320 kW, i7 728 km WLTP. EU and US buyers are turning to hybrids | McKinsey CN 2025, Deloitte 2026 | [S56][S61][S13][S9] |
| Feature monetisation | Subscriptions for hardware already in the car are rejected. BMW dropped the heated-seat subscription (2023) because "people feel they paid double" | BMW exec | [S62] |
| Brand loyalty eroding | 34% of premium drivers are open to switching vs 25% mass-market. The premium vs mass "emotional satisfaction gap" is narrowing (J.D. Power APEAL 2026) | McKinsey 2026 | [S43] |
| Affordability | Downsizing and delay; value scrutiny even in premium | Deloitte 2026, McKinsey 2026 | [S61][S43] |
| Interior / sustainability | High-end materials are the #2 purchase criterion (48%) for luxury buyers, and sustainability is a top-3 differentiation wish **(2022 data, U for 2030)** | McKinsey luxury survey via leatherbiz | [S63] |
| Personalisation | Driver profiles and smart preferences are among the top-rated tech **(U as a WTP signal)** | J.D. Power TXI | [S58] |

## 4. Brand positioning

| Brand | What customers expect / perceive | Src |
|---|---|---|
| **BMW (stated)** | "Sheer Driving Pleasure" ("Freude am Fahren"; US: "The Ultimate Driving Machine" **(U, not fetched)**). Neue Klasse adds "Heart of Joy" (driving dynamics as the 4th pillar beside electric, digital, circular). Zipse: "Sheer Driving Pleasure – taken to a whole new level" | [S64][S65] |
| BMW (perceived) | Sportiness, driver focus, dynamics; M brand strong (213,457, record). Design controversies: big kidney grilles (XM, 7 Series, 4 Series), which BMW says were driven by China demand and that "complainers are often not customers". 7 Series facelift moves to horizontal slats | [S1][S66][S9] |
| **Mercedes** | Luxury, comfort, prestige, screens (Superscreen), rear-seat opulence (Maybach); leads on LLM assistant and illuminated design | [S34] |
| **Audi** | Tech-understated, quattro, quality. A6L wins on value and space in China; separate China EV brand | [S4][S20] |
| **Tesla** | Software, efficiency, charging network, FSD; ageing line-up (Model S ends 2026) | [S22][S17] |
| **Porsche** | Sporty luxury; #1 US APEAL premium brand | [S36] |
| **Lexus** | Reliability, quiet comfort, value-luxury | [S32] |
| **Chinese (Huawei/HIMA, Xiaomi, NIO, Li)** | Tech-first: ADAS, smart cockpit, ecosystem, rear-seat entertainment, value, speed of updates | [S54][S56][S29] |

### Brand-fit guardrails (for `fit_checks.brand`)

**All segments**
- **Fits BMW (pass):** precise steering and handling, rear-wheel-drive-biased feel and xDrive, responsive powertrains; driver-centric HMI (head-up display, Panoramic Vision, physical shortcut controls, iDrive-style haptic control); efficiency and range as "dynamics"; sporty-elegant design; M and M Performance variants; high-quality OTA and natural voice that *works*; ADAS that reduces burden while keeping the driver in charge.
- **Warn:** features that are "comfort-only" with no link to driving pleasure (acceptable but not differentiating); market-specific ecosystem partners (Huawei/Alibaba) acceptable in China only; grille-size escalation (polarising; region-specific).
- **Fail (contradicts the brand):** paywalling hardware already in the car (heated-seat precedent); touch-only access to core driving functions; soft, numb chassis tuning as default; gimmick recognition tech with no customer problem; copying the Chinese "living room on wheels" so far that the driver role is diminished in the 1 and 5 Series.

| Segment | Fits BMW (pass) | Warn | Contradicts (fail) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1 Series** | Hot-hatch driving fun (M135), compact premium quality, intuitive physical controls, efficient BEV/PHEV option, youthful digital UX and app ecosystem | Pure value or feature stuffing to fight Chinese entrants; FWD-only perception | Cheap interior trim; touch-only climate (already criticised); losing dynamic edge vs Golf GTI |
| **5 Series / i5** | "Business athlete": dynamics plus long-distance comfort, top ADAS on the highway, fast charging and range, rear comfort in the China LWB, quiet cabin | China-only rear "boss" features in the G68 (pass for CN, warn for EU/US); third-party cockpit OS (CN only) | Sacrificing handling for float-ride everywhere; global commitment to an EREV range-extender identity **(PM judgement)** |
| **7 Series / i7** | Driver-*and*-chauffeur duality, Theatre Screen and rear lounge, Executive Lounge seats, craftsmanship, quiet BEV, L2+/L3 assisted driving | Matching Maextro/M9 gadgets one-for-one (fridge, projector) unless executed at BMW quality | Overt bling with no taste (grille-size controversy); dropping driving dynamics entirely (the S-Class owns pure comfort) |

input.message:
I wrote `/Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final/foundation/documents/competitor-landscape.md` and touched no other file. It covers all four parts of the brief, and every fact links to one of 66 numbered sources with URL and publication date. Unverified, single-source or conflicting items are marked **(U)** or "(conflict)".

**What the file contains:**
- **Baseline:** BMW's 2025 numbers, plus what is known per model.
- **Competitor tables per segment (1 Series, 5 Series / i5 / G68, 7 Series / i7):** 2025 sales where available and the strengths customers cite. The Chinese rivals included are Xiaomi, AITO/HIMA, Maextro, NIO, Xpeng, Li Auto, Zeekr, Avatr, Yangwang and Hongqi.
- **Demand trends:** EU, US and China powertrain and body-style shares, plus six evidence-backed reasons Chinese premium brands are taking share in China.
- **Customer expectations 2025–2030:** from J.D. Power (China and US tech studies), McKinsey (China 2025, global consumer survey 2026), Deloitte 2026 and Euro NCAP 2026.
- **Brand positioning:** BMW's own stated values ("Sheer Driving Pleasure" and "Heart of Joy", the dynamics control unit BMW calls the fourth Neue Klasse pillar), how competitors are perceived, and a brand-fit guardrail list (pass / warn / fail) per segment that maps onto the brand-fit check in the requirement model.
- **Known gaps** at the end.

**Data caveats:**
- **Model-level sales are patchy.** BMW does not break out 1, 5 or 7 Series full-year 2025 sales by region, so I used partial periods (5 Series in Europe Jan–Apr, China Jan–Nov) and a December 2025 China snapshot for the 7 Series.
- **Conflicting figures shown side by side:**
  - Mercedes in China: 551,900 (Mercedes) vs 472,799 (Inovev).
  - Xiaomi SU7: 258,164 vs 256,164.
- **Weaker sources:**
  - The 2024 US 7 Series and S-Class numbers come from a forum post.
  - The roughly 41% domestic share of China's over-RMB-300k market comes from a garbled page.

**Most decision-relevant insights:**
1. BMW's China sales fell 12.5% in 2025 (Mercedes −19%, Porsche −26%) while Europe grew 7.3% and the US 5%. China is where the successor requirements are most at risk.
2. In China's premium segment, domestic brands rose from 24.9% (2023) to about 41% (2025, unverified). Above RMB 300k, they hold over 80% of electric and plug-in sales.
3. Assisted driving is the main reason Chinese premium buyers switch. It is their top purchase reason, and 50% would change brand for better ADAS, against about 25% globally. Smart cockpit and ecosystem come second.
4. In the luxury segment, Huawei's Maextro S800 outsold Panamera, 7 Series and Maybach S combined in December 2025 (4,376 vs 4,140). It wins on a long wheelbase, rear-seat tech and Huawei ADS at RMB 708k–1.018M.
5. Among German C-segment sedans in China, the 5 Series ranks third (Jan–Nov: A6L 147.8k, E-Class 117.6k, 5 Series 107.3k). The i5 sold only 6,379 there in 2025, and its China production reportedly ends in July 2026.
6. In Europe the 5 Series leads its segment and the 1 Series grew 9.5%. But SUVs are about 59% of the market, sedans 3.5%, and premium mid-size sedans fell 19% (Jan–Oct 2025). The successor case leans on core loyalists plus the China LWB.
7. The US electric share collapsed to under 6% after the federal credit ended, so US successors need strong plug-in hybrid and combustion offers. EU electric share is 17.4% and rising; China is about 54% NEV, with range-extenders gaining.
8. Tech has to work, not just exist. J.D. Power finds cockpit usability is over a third of tech problems. Euro NCAP 2026 rewards physical controls, and the F70 was already criticised for touch-only climate controls.
9. Mercedes is moving fast on software: MB.OS with over-the-air updates and ChatGPT/Gemini in the CLA and the 2026 S-Class, with its advanced assisted driving launching in China first. The 7 Series facelift has Alexa+ but no Level 3 claim. AI voice and reliable over-the-air updates are becoming table stakes.
10. Brand guardrails: driving pleasure plus intuitive driver-focused tech fits BMW. Charging subscriptions for hardware already in the car fails (BMW dropped the heated-seat subscription in 2023 because "people feel they paid double"), as do touch-only core controls and diluted dynamics. China-specific rear-seat and ecosystem features should pass only as China variants (G68, 7 Series China).
